dedupe_keys.name: patient flow network analysis of two uk acute hospitals r code reproducing the plos one study of sub networks linked to a e performance

description: This R code reproduces the analysis in the PLOS ONE paper Network analysis of patient flow in two UK acute care hospitals identifies key sub-networks for A&E performance. The study treated the wards and units of two UK acute hospitals as a network through which patients move, and identified the parts of that network whose flow is linked to performance of the accident and emergency department. The work was led from King's College London with funding from the National Institute for Health Research biomedical research centres and the Farr Institute, and the contact is Dan Bean. The code is free to download from GitHub under the GPL-3.0 licence. Caveats: the hospital patient data behind the paper are not described as included, so users need their own ward movement records, and the repository is a reproduction of one study, not a maintained package. Coverage is two acute hospitals in the United Kingdom, with methods applicable elsewhere. Simulation uses: finding internal bottlenecks, such as wards whose congestion slows emergency department discharges, before modelling hospital capacity under surges. Related records: the NHS trust classification (data-nhs-trust-classification-england) describes the English acute trusts to which such analyses apply.
inputs: Patient movements between wards and units within a hospital
name: Patient flow network analysis of two UK acute hospitals: R code reproducing the PLOS ONE study of sub-networks linked to A&E performance
outputs: Patient flow network and the sub-networks associated with A&E (emergency department) performance
provider: Dan Bean (King's College London) and co-authors
